title: Knowing the way is not the same as being guided
subtitle: Al-Hadi: the Guide who shows the path and moves the heart to walk it
intro: Al-Hadi (الْهَادِي) means The Guide: the One who guides every creature to what is good for it, shows people the path through their nature and through revelation, and alone places guidance in the heart so that it accepts and acts. It is the one dua every Muslim makes at least seventeen times a day. And guidance has doors you can knock on.

root.sense: Hidayah is guiding someone gently to where they need to go, showing the way and leading along it. Hadiyyah, a gift, comes from the same root. Al-Hadi is the One who directs each creature to its good, and the hearts of His servants to Him.

row.title: When Allah guides me, I'll change

knowing: Al-Hadi guides on several levels. First, every creature: our Lord is He who gave each thing its form, then guided it (20:50), the bee to its flower, the newborn to its mother. Then every human: He gave us eyes, ears, a mind, and a built-in longing for meaning, like apps installed on a phone that cannot be removed. Then revelation: messengers and a Book that show the road like signs on a motorway.

But signs cannot grab the wheel. {idea}The deepest level, guidance that enters the heart so it accepts and acts, belongs to Allah alone{/idea}. That is why Allah told the Prophet ﷺ both that you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills (28:56), and that you do guide to a straight path (42:52). He shows the way; only Allah moves the heart.

This is also why {trap}knowledge alone is not guidance{/trap}. Pharaoh knew Musa's signs were true. Some People of the Book recognised the Prophet ﷺ and still refused. Arrogance, envy and a hard heart can block everything. Allah sufficed the Prophet ﷺ as a Guide and a Helper (25:31).
seeing: Nuh called to his son as the waves rose like mountains: come aboard with us. The son said a mountain would protect him, and the waves came between them (11:42-43). The Prophet ﷺ pleaded with his uncle Abu Talib, who had protected him for years, to say the testimony before he died; he did not. These are the most painful scenes in the Quran's story of guidance, and they teach parents and friends alike that {idea}we can show the way, but the heart is His{/idea}.

Then there are Pharaoh's magicians. The moment they saw the truth, they fell in prostration, and when threatened with crucifixion they said: never will we prefer you over the clear proofs that came to us and the One who created us (20:70-72). One sincere step, and Al-Hadi gave them a certainty that nothing could shake.
trusting: No one waits on the sofa for wealth to fall from the sky, yet many treat guidance as random. The Quran shows its means. Ask: in a hadith qudsi in Sahih Muslim, Allah says all of you are astray except whom I guide, so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you. Strive: those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways (29:69); fighting your own habits is that striving. Trust Him when the right path costs you. And keep returning: He guides to Himself whoever turns back to Him (13:27).

Guidance does not mean never falling. It means getting back up each time, like a sat nav that loses signal and then says: there is a way back. {reward}Measure your guidance by how often you return{/reward}, not by how perfect you are. And give Him the credit for every good you do: the people of Paradise will say, we would never have been guided had Allah not guided us (7:43). That keeps you humble, and stops you looking down on anyone still finding their way.
loving: Think of where you could be right now without His guidance. Every prayer you have prayed was an invitation He extended and helped you accept. {reward}A heart that sees this loves Al-Hadi as a lost child loves the hand that led it home{/reward}.
now: Your son has not prayed in months and laughed when you mentioned it at dinner. You lie awake replaying everything you said wrong. You can show him the way, love him, and pray for him; you cannot place guidance in his heart. Hand that part to Al-Hadi tonight in sujud.
old: I think guidance is something that will happen to me one day, or that my knowledge already guarantees it.
new: Al-Hadi places guidance in the heart, and I reach for it by asking, striving, trusting and returning.
try: In every rak'ah today, slow down at ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim and mean it, asking for guidance in one specific thing you are struggling with.

dua.text: Ya Hadi, guide me to the straight path, guide me to the best of character, for none guides to it but You, and keep my heart firm after You have guided it.
dua.note: The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah in his opening prayer to guide him to the best of character, since none guides to it but He (Sahih Muslim).

pairs.why: An-Nur lights the path so it can be seen; Al-Hadi leads you along it and opens your heart to walk it.
Al-Hadi shows and gives the way; Ar-Rashid directs every affair to its right end with perfect wisdom.
Allah is the protecting Friend of believers, bringing them out of darkness, and guidance is how He does it.

faq.a: Al-Hadi means The Guide. Allah guides every creature to what benefits it, shows humanity the way through their nature and through revelation, and alone gives the inner guidance that makes a heart accept the truth and act on it.

faq.q: Can a person guide someone else?
faq.a: People can show the way and call to it; the Quran says the Prophet ﷺ guides to a straight path (42:52). But placing guidance in the heart belongs to Allah alone: you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills (28:56).

faq.q: How do I get guidance from Allah?
faq.a: Ask for it sincerely, as in al-Fatihah and the hadith qudsi in Sahih Muslim; strive against your own desires (29:69); trust Him when the right path is costly; and keep turning back to Him after every slip, since He guides those who return (13:27).
